title: Night waking: half your bed is his
angle: [F1 HPSPC] Problem: at 2am she's half asleep, and letting him in is the only easy choice; by morning she's on the edge of her own bed. Solution: (1) decide what you'll do at 2am *before* the night, so you're not deciding half asleep; (2) walk him back every time with the same two words, e.g. "يلا سريرك", lights low, no talk; (3) if you need to stay, sit by *his* bed and don't lie down. Proof: the method line. CTA (Reflection): the 2am visit is one moment of many; the assessment shows where to start.
hook_ar: سريرك صار نصه لطفلك؟ كل ليلة الساعة اثنين يجي ينام جنبك؟
hook_gloss: Your bed has become half your child's? Every night at two he comes to sleep beside you?

title: Sneaking out: he opens his eyes
angle: [F2 Story] Story beats: the hour, sliding her arm out, the floor creaks, his eyes open, back to zero. Turn: he fell asleep with you there, so when he half-wakes and you're gone, it's a new place. Move (not the chair method): tell him "برجع لك بعد شوي" and leave while he's still awake, then really come back after a minute, then two, then five. He learns you come back. CTA (Observation): notice how he falls asleep each night; those details build the plan.
hook_ar: جلستي ساعة  تنوميه، وأول ما قُمتي من جمبه فتح عيونه؟
hook_gloss: You sat an hour getting him to sleep, and the moment you got up from beside him he opened his eyes?

title: Your evening: 8 to 10
angle: [F6 Checklist] Self-check, one part per slide: (1) what time did his afternoon nap end? (2) what was the last thing he did before pyjamas (screen, running around, a bath)? (3) did bedtime move tonight because of a visit or guests? One small move for each. The «رؤوس أقلام» are the three checks themselves. CTA = Anhar's own: «لاحظي ايش يصير خلال اليوم قبل وقت النوم…».
hook_ar: تبدئي تنوميه الساعة ثمانيه، وما تطلعي من غرفته إلا الساعة عشره؟
hook_gloss: You start putting him to sleep at eight, and you don't leave his room until ten?

title: "Just today" became every night
angle: [F3 Two voices] Two voices: the her of that night («اليوم بس، تعبانة») and the her of now. Normalise: it wasn't wrong. Move (new): start with the **afternoon nap** in his own bed, not the night; the day is easier for both of you. Then the same two words at night, and return him without lying down again. CTA (Direct).
hook_ar: قلتي له اليوم بس تنام جنبي، ودحين ما يرضى ينام لحاله؟
hook_gloss: You told him 'just today you'll sleep beside me', and now he refuses to sleep on his own?

title: Cooking: he hangs on you
angle: [F1 HPSPC] Problem: he wants *you*, not the kitchen; cooking at night costs her sleep. Seconds-long moves, zero prep: (1) one low kitchen drawer that's his (plastic containers, wooden spoons); (2) a job beside you, away from the stove: washing cucumbers in a bowl of water; (3) say out loud what you're doing ("دحين بنقطع البصل"), so he's with you without being on you. Proof: method. CTA (Direct).
hook_ar: أول ما تدخلي المطبخ يتعلق فيكي، فصرتي تطبخي غدا بكرة وهو نايم؟
hook_gloss: As soon as you enter the kitchen he clings to you, so now you cook tomorrow's lunch while he's asleep?

title: Only after he sleeps
angle: [F6 Checklist] Checklist build: the 'after he sleeps' list she's built (vacuum, cooking, a shower, a call). Turn: you don't need to win them all back, just one. Moves: pick the shortest; do it at the same time each day so he knows it's coming; give him a part in it (he presses the button, carries the dustpan). CTA (Reflection): which one weighs most? The assessment helps set the starting point.
hook_ar: ما تقدري تكنسي وهو صاحي، ولا تطبخي إلا بعد ما ينام؟
hook_gloss: You can't vacuum while he's awake, and you don't cook until after he sleeps?

title: Hair dryer: only when he's far
angle: [F5 Walk-through] Walking listicle, a twist in each: (1) not 'warn him first' (she's heard it) but let him see it *off* first and hold it; (2) start on the lowest setting, pointed away from him, from across the room; (3) he's the one who presses the button. Fast close + CTA (Direct).
hook_ar: ما تقدري تشغلي الاستشوار إلا لما يكون طفلك بعيد عنك؟
hook_gloss: You can't turn on the hair dryer unless your child is far from you?

title: Blender: make sure he's far
angle: [F2 Story] Story: she wants a juice, checks where he is, waits, he walks in, she gives up, puts it back. Moves (seconds): a folded towel under the blender (it really is quieter); short pulses instead of one long run; he sees it before it starts. CTA (Observation): notice which sounds he moves away from and which he doesn't.
hook_ar: كل ما تبغي تشغلي الخلاط، لازم تتأكدي إن طفلك بعيد؟
hook_gloss: Every time you want to turn on the blender, you have to make sure your child is far away?

title: Shower: knocking and crying
angle: [F3 Two voices] Two voices: him at the door, her inside rushing. Moves: (1) shower right after he's started something he likes, not when he's free; (2) keep talking or singing through the door so he hears you're there; (3) give him a job: he holds your towel outside and hands it to you when you come out. CTA (Reflection).
hook_ar: يدق باب الحمام ويبكي  أول ما تسكريه، فصرتي تتروشي بعد ما ينام أو قبل ما يصحى؟
hook_gloss: He knocks on the bathroom door and cries the moment you close it, so now you shower after he sleeps or before he wakes?

title: Hair wash: you come out wetter
angle: [F5 Walk-through] Walk-through with twists: (1) a dry face towel he holds over his own eyes; (2) count out loud to the same number every time, then stop ("لين عشرة"), so he knows when it ends; (3) let him hold the shower head. Fast close + CTA (Observation).
hook_ar: تغسلي شعره وهو يصيح، وتطلعي من الحمام وأنتي اللي مبلولة أكثر منه؟
hook_gloss: You wash his hair while he screams, and you come out of the bathroom wetter than him?

title: Kids' salon: screaming and running
angle: [F1 HPSPC] Problem: the whole visit is a battle, and she leaves with half a haircut. Moves: (1) حاولي the quietest time (weekday morning); (2) the first time, just sit and watch another child, no haircut; (3) let him feel the clipper's buzz on your arm, then his hand, before his head; (4) something of his own to hold. Proof: method. CTA (Direct).
hook_ar: كل ما وديتيه صالون الاطفال، يبدأ الصراخ ويحاول يهرب؟
hook_gloss: Every time you take him to the kids' salon, the screaming starts and he tries to run?

title: Phone calls: only behind a locked door
angle: [F4 Metaphor] Metaphor from his side: on the phone you're in front of him, but your voice and eyes went somewhere else, like when someone talks to you while looking at their phone. Moves: (1) a small box of things that only comes out during calls; (2) let him say hi to grandma on speaker first; (3) keep a hand on him while you talk. CTA (Reflection).
hook_ar: ما تقدري تكملي مكالمة مع أمك إلا لما تدخلي الحمام وتقفلي الباب؟
hook_gloss: You can't finish a call with your mum unless you go into the bathroom and lock the door?
